title: A Comparative Study of Fifteen Techniques for the Early Sizing of Software Requirements
content: Early Software Sizing (ESS) techniques address the challenge of estimating software size early in the development life cycle when detailed requirements are incomplete or unavailable. This study presents a quantitative comparison of fifteen ESS techniques developed by the COSMIC Group and applied to the ‘Course Registration’ case study. It evaluates the size variations, applicability, and limitations of these ESS techniques using two comparison protocols. The first protocol uses the synthetic early size scales documented in the COSMIC Early Software Sizing Guides. The second protocol uses a training-testing approach to use a local early size scale derived from a portion of a local dataset. In this case study, the mean absolute variation was about 22% with synthetic scales and about 14% with local scales, and the Average of use cases technique showed the highest variation in both protocols. This evaluation offers insights into the strengths and constraints of each ESS technique, supporting practitioners and researchers in selecting the appropriate ESS techniques.
